title: A Round Robin characterisation of the hydrogen sorption properties of a carbon based material
material_description: CMS 4A / participant 1 | Takeda Chem. Ind. carbon molecular sieve CMS 4A (commercial microporous carbon, extruded cylindrical pellets ~2.2 mm diameter), Round Robin material distributed to all participants; H2 measured by participant 1 (volumetric static)
source_location: si1 p.2, Supplementary Table 1 (H2 uptake at 77 K from interpolated adsorption isotherms), row 1, 0.1 MPa column
notes: pressure printed as 0.1 MPa; value stated to be taken from the interpolated adsorption isotherm at a fixed pressure (SI caption; Sect. 7.3/7.5); no plotted point of this isotherm was identified within 2% of this pressure; isotherm_point_count is the minimum number of markers identified on the plot; further markers near the origin overlap with other isotherms and could not be counted; Round Robin (NESSHY) material Takeda CMS 4A; participant code 1 (Volumetric static); laboratory identity anonymised in the paper. BET 423 (+/-20) m2/g and DR apparent micropore volume 1.7 (+/-0.1) x 10^-4 m3/kg (= 0.17 cm3/g) from N2 at 77 K, measured by the RRT organisers on the RRT material; BET range not stated. Outgassing per RRT protocol (all participants): 383 K for 24 h then 523 K (249.85 C) for 4 h under dynamic high vacuum (protocol: below 10^-3 Pa); final outgassing pressure 8 x 10^-4 Pa as printed (Table 1). sample_mass_mg = initial weight before outgassing (Table 1), weight loss 2.5%. He sample density 2.72 x 10^3 kg/m3 (Volumetric). Equilibrium time 15 (77 K) / 15 (ambient) min; temperature stability Nr / Nr; EOS Real; pressure transducer accuracy 0.02 %FS (Table 1). Basis: paper states H2 adsorption corresponds to excess adsorption (Sect. 4.1), not defined; basis_inferred = excess by that naming. replicates_reported = true: the same sample was measured independently by 14 laboratories (round robin); no per-laboratory uncertainty given.
basis_evidence: "The adsorption of hydrogen on porous materials corresponds to an excess adsorption, which is the only experimentally accessible variable by all conventional techniques [1,3,13]." (main p.3046, Sect. 4.1)
free_volume_calibration: He expansion in the volumetric instrument at room temperature (sample density 2.72 x 10^3 kg/m3; Sect. 7.1.3)
material_identity: Takeda Chem. Ind. Japan; carbon molecular sieve CMS 4A

source_location: si1 p.4, Supplementary Table 3 (H2 uptake at ambient temperature from interpolated adsorption isotherms), row 1, 5.0 MPa column
notes: pressure printed as 5.0 MPa; value stated to be taken from the interpolated adsorption isotherm at a fixed pressure (SI caption; Sect. 7.3/7.5); no plotted point of this isotherm was identified within 2% of this pressure (at ambient temperature only the highest-pressure point was digitized); isotherm_point_count is the minimum number of markers identified on the plot; further markers near the origin overlap with other isotherms and could not be counted; Round Robin (NESSHY) material Takeda CMS 4A; participant code 1 (Volumetric static); laboratory identity anonymised in the paper. BET 423 (+/-20) m2/g and DR apparent micropore volume 1.7 (+/-0.1) x 10^-4 m3/kg (= 0.17 cm3/g) from N2 at 77 K, measured by the RRT organisers on the RRT material; BET range not stated. Outgassing per RRT protocol (all participants): 383 K for 24 h then 523 K (249.85 C) for 4 h under dynamic high vacuum (protocol: below 10^-3 Pa); final outgassing pressure 8 x 10^-4 Pa as printed (Table 1). sample_mass_mg = initial weight before outgassing (Table 1), weight loss 2.5%. He sample density 2.72 x 10^3 kg/m3 (Volumetric). Equilibrium time 15 (77 K) / 15 (ambient) min; temperature stability Nr / Nr; EOS Real; pressure transducer accuracy 0.02 %FS (Table 1). Basis: paper states H2 adsorption corresponds to excess adsorption (Sect. 4.1), not defined; basis_inferred = excess by that naming. replicates_reported = true: the same sample was measured independently by 14 laboratories (round robin); no per-laboratory uncertainty given.
basis_evidence: "The adsorption of hydrogen on porous materials corresponds to an excess adsorption, which is the only experimentally accessible variable by all conventional techniques [1,3,13]." (main p.3046, Sect. 4.1)
free_volume_calibration: He expansion in the volumetric instrument at room temperature (sample density 2.72 x 10^3 kg/m3; Sect. 7.1.3)
material_identity: Takeda Chem. Ind. Japan; carbon molecular sieve CMS 4A
